---
title: "STAC"
---

Fair Data Finder exposes domains and datasets through a
[STAC](https://stacspec.org/) API built on
[stac-fastapi](https://github.com/stac-utils/stac-fastapi) and
[pgSTAC](https://github.com/stac-utils/pgstac).

Official references:

- [STAC specification](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-spec)
- [STAC API specification](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-api-spec)
- [STAC Item Search](https://api.stacspec.org/v1.0.0/item-search/)
- [STAC Filter Extension (CQL2)](https://github.com/stac-api-extensions/filter)

## What is STAC?

**STAC** (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) is an open specification for
describing geospatial datasets so that they can be searched and accessed in a
consistent way.

It solves a common problem: every portal invents its own metadata shape and
search API. STAC defines shared JSON structures and HTTP patterns so clients
(and humans) can discover **what data exists**, **where and when it applies**,
and **how to open it**.

Fair Data Finder uses STAC so that:

- Domains and datasets have a standard JSON representation
- Search can use standard Item Search + CQL2 filters
- Data access links are modelled as Assets
- The same records power the UI and external API consumers

### Main STAC concepts

| Concept | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **Catalog** | Entry point that links to collections and other resources |
| **Collection** | Group of related Items, with its own metadata and extent |
| **Item** | One dataset record (a GeoJSON Feature with STAC fields) |
| **Asset** | A downloadable or browsable resource (`href`) attached to an Item |
| **Spatial extent** | Geographic coverage (Collection extent and/or Item `geometry` / `bbox`) |
| **Temporal extent** | Time coverage (Collection interval and/or Item `datetime` / start–end) |

This page does not reproduce the full specification — use the links above for
normative detail.

## STAC in Fair Data Finder

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Cat[STAC Catalog<br/>GET /api/]
  Col[Collection<br/>= Domain]
  Item[Item<br/>= Dataset]
  Asset[Asset<br/>= data access href]
  Fac[Facility keywords<br/>public schema]

  Cat --> Col
  Col --> Item
  Item --> Asset
  Fac -.->|Collection link rel=keywords| Col
  Fac -.->|copied to properties.keywords| Item
```

| FDF concept | STAC representation |
|-------------|---------------------|
| Catalog root | `GET /api/` |
| Domain | Collection |
| Dataset / registered record | Item |
| File or service link | Asset on the Item |
| Keyword vocabulary | Application API (`/facility`, `/keywords`, …), linked from the Collection |
| Keywords on a dataset | `properties.keywords` (array of objects) |
| Project number | `properties.projectNumber` (custom property) |

### Notable FDF behaviours

- **Null geometry is allowed.** Items without geometry are valid and appear
  in Search as global datasets.
- **Domain ↔ keywords link** uses a Collection link with `rel: "keywords"`
  pointing at a Facility id — this is application-specific, not a core STAC
  relation.
- **Many descriptive fields** are custom properties under `properties`
  (see [Metadata schema](metadata-schema.qmd)).
- **RBAC** restricts who may create/update/delete Collections and Items;
  authenticating is still required to call almost all STAC routes.

## Using the STAC API

All routes are served under the `/api` root path (configurable via
`STAC_FASTAPI_ROOT_PATH`, default `/api`).

Interactive OpenAPI / Swagger UI is available at `{API}/api.html` when the
backend is running. Below, `{API}` means your Fair Data Finder base URL (for
example `https://your-fdf-instance.example.com/api`).

### Authentication

Almost all STAC endpoints require a logged-in session. Fair Data Finder
authenticates with an HTTP **cookie** named `DMS_TOKEN` (a JWT issued after
Microsoft SSO login). This is **not** a Bearer token in an `Authorization`
header.

Public exceptions (no cookie required):

| Method | Path |
|--------|------|
| `GET` | `/` (catalog landing page) |
| `GET` | `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/callback`, `/auth/me` |

Obtain a token by signing in through the UI (`/api/auth/login`). The browser
stores `DMS_TOKEN` automatically. For scripted access, pass the same cookie:

```bash
curl \
  -H "Cookie: DMS_TOKEN=$DMS_TOKEN" \
  "{API}/collections"
```

Do not commit real tokens. Treat `$DMS_TOKEN` as a secret.

::: {.callout-important}
Calls to `/search`, `/collections`, and item routes without a valid
`DMS_TOKEN` cookie return **401 Unauthorized**.
:::

### Endpoints

#### Catalog

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/` |
| **Auth** | Public |
| **Description** | STAC Catalog landing page (conformance links, child links) |

#### Conformance

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/conformance` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | Lists implemented STAC API conformance classes |

#### Collections

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/collections` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | List domains (Collections) |

```bash
curl -H "Cookie: DMS_TOKEN=$DMS_TOKEN" "{API}/collections"
```

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `POST {API}/collections` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` + `collection:create` |
| **Description** | Create a domain |

#### Individual collection

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/collections/{collection_id}` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | Fetch one domain |

```bash
curl -H "Cookie: DMS_TOKEN=$DMS_TOKEN" \
  "{API}/collections/ecology"
```

Also supported with appropriate permissions: `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` on
`/collections/{collection_id}`.

#### Items in a collection

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/collections/{collection_id}/items` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | List datasets in a domain |

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `POST {API}/collections/{collection_id}/items` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` + `item:create` on that collection |
| **Description** | Register a dataset |

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET {API}/collections/{collection_id}/items/{item_id}` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | Fetch one dataset |

Also supported with permissions: `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` on the item path,
and `POST /collections/{collection_id}/bulk_items` for bulk writes.

#### Search

Implements [STAC API Item Search](https://api.stacspec.org/v1.0.0/item-search/).

| | |
|--|--|
| **Method / path** | `GET` or `POST {API}/search` |
| **Auth** | Requires `DMS_TOKEN` |
| **Description** | Search datasets across collections |

Common body fields: `collections`, `bbox`, `intersects`, `datetime`,
`limit`, `fields`, `sortby`, `token`, `filter`, `filter-lang`.

**Unfiltered search** (omit `filter` entirely):

```bash
curl -X POST "{API}/search" \
  -H "Cookie: DMS_TOKEN=$DMS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"limit": 500}'
```

**CQL2 JSON filter** (`filter-lang: cql2-json`), as used by the UI:

```bash
curl -X POST "{API}/search" \
  -H "Cookie: DMS_TOKEN=$DMS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "filter-lang": "cql2-json",
    "filter": {
      "op": "and",
      "args": [
        {
          "op": "like",
          "args": [{ "property": "properties.title" }, "%water%"]
        },
        {
          "op": "a_overlaps",
          "args": [
            { "property": "properties.keywords.id" },
            ["0898e009-a91d-4589-8adc-837178859c73"]
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

Operators used by Fair Data Finder include `and`, `or`, `like`, `>=`, `<=`,
`s_intersects`, `a_overlaps`, and `isNull`. Array-valued keyword ids must use
`a_overlaps`, not `in`.

Queryable properties are advertised at `{API}/queryables`.

#### Queryables and health

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `{API}/queryables` | Properties available for CQL2 filters |
| `GET` | `{API}/_mgmt/health` | Health check |
| `GET` | `{API}/_mgmt/ping` | Ping |

### Example Item shape (illustrative)

```json
{
  "type": "Feature",
  "stac_version": "1.0.0",
  "id": "V1StGXR8_Z5jdHi6B-myT",
  "collection": "ecology",
  "geometry": null,
  "bbox": null,
  "properties": {
    "title": "Example dataset",
    "projectNumber": "1234567",
    "description": "…",
    "datetime": "2024-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    "keywords": [
      {
        "id": "0898e009-a91d-4589-8adc-837178859c73",
        "nl_keyword": "Voorbeeld",
        "en_keyword": "Example"
      }
    ]
  },
  "assets": {
    "data": {
      "title": "Dataset",
      "href": "https://example.invalid/data.zip",
      "type": "application/zip"
    }
  },
  "links": []
}
```

For the full application API surface (auth, keywords, groups), see
[API](api.qmd).
